title: Hand-written static site with no defects
notes:
The primary control. Nothing here is wrong, so every finding is a false positive and the case exists to measure exactly that. A registry of 224 requirements evaluated against a small correct site is where an over-eager rule shows itself: a check that fires on a well-formed page would be indistinguishable, in a report, from a check that found a real problem, and an autonomous agent acting on it would damage working code.

The fixture deliberately supplies the resources the optional checks look for - a robots.txt, a sitemap, an RSS feed, and an llms.txt - so those checks inspect something and pass rather than reporting NOT_APPLICABLE. That is what makes them count toward the true-negative denominator.

Six checks still report NOT_APPLICABLE and are absent from expected_non_findings on purpose. There is no separate rendered capture, so the initial and executed documents were never compared; there are no hreflang alternates; and there is no review or rating markup. Listing those six would claim credit for four comparisons that never happened and two that had nothing to examine.
expected_not_applicable_rationale: The same exclusions as defective-static, asserted here because a control that only proves "no findings" would not catch a rule being offered to a site that cannot act on it. A requirement selected for the wrong site is a false positive that has not happened yet.
expected_applicable_rationale: A plain static site establishes only the universal fact plus the three it establishes by shipping files. These are deliberately modest assertions: their value is that they hold on the simplest possible project, so a selector that had quietly started requiring a framework would fail here first.
